CounterCoverage.description:
How much of the fabric the window actually saw.

`unsupported` is fabric-level and per counter, because a counter no port can
report is a property of the hardware rather than of any one port -- and
saying it once keeps it off every port row. It is what lets the UI grey
out a checkbox instead of showing a column of honest, useless zeros.
CounterCoverage.title: CounterCoverage

CounterWindow.description:
Which readings actually bounded the delta.

Requested and observed instants are both present and they differ, because
counters are sampled discretely: a request for 09:00 is answered by whatever
reading sat nearest it. A client drawing a per-hour figure from a span that
is not quite an hour is wrong, and without this cannot know it.
CounterWindow.title: CounterWindow

Diff.description:
The union of both endpoints' topologies, annotated.

Union rather than a change-list: a removed link is absent from the `to`
topology, so a client given only the changes could not draw the ghost.

`churn` counts events regardless of net change, because a link that flapped
repeatedly and came back is byte-identical in a net diff and is probably the
most interesting thing in the range.

`system_groups` is the union of both endpoints', so a chassis that lost its
last node is still there for the removed children to sit inside.
Diff.title: Diff

Head.description: Cheap poll target. Refetch topology only when topology_hash moves.
Head.title: Head

Peer.description: The far end of a port's link, resolved so a panel needs no second fetch.
Peer.title: Peer

PortErrorDelta.description:
One port's accumulation over the window.

Sparse in two directions: `d` carries only counters that moved, and a port
with nothing to say is absent entirely. That deliberately inverts the
storage decision -- the schema stores dense because columnar compression
rewards it, while the wire is sparse because the client already holds the
port universe and a healthy fabric is nearly all zeros.

Absence therefore means zero, which is only safe because every case where it
would instead mean *unknown* raises a flag below.

Every field below `port` keeps a default and the route serialises with
`exclude_defaults`, so a clean row is `{"node", "port", "d"}`. The
envelope's fields stay required so the same switch cannot elide a zero that
means something.
PortErrorDelta.title: PortErrorDelta

PortRate.description:
One port's throughput over a trailing window, for a detail card.

Separate from `PortTraffic`, the overlay's sparse wire shape. This one is
already attached to the port it describes, so it carries no identity and
elides nothing -- an idle port on a card reads "0.00 Gbps" rather than
vanishing the way it does from the overlay payload.
PortRate.title: PortRate

PortTraffic.description:
One port's rate over the window.

Gbps on the wire rather than raw octets: the conversion needs `xmit_data`'s
x4 scaling, the span, and the knowledge that these are wire bytes -- three
things the server has and a client would have to be told.

Sparse on a floor rather than on a flag, because traffic is genuinely dense
where errors are not. An omitted port is below `IDLE_FLOOR_GBPS` and reads
as idle either way, which is most of the payload at a 5 s cadence.
PortTraffic.title: PortTraffic

Rate.description: A speed or width, as stored and as read.
Rate.title: Rate

Resolved.description:
Which sweep answered this request. Present on every time-parameterised
response.

Built from the `db.Resolved` dataclass the pool hands back.
Resolved.title: Resolved

Snapshots.description:
Written unconditionally by the collector, so a gap in this 
list is a collector outage rather than a quiet fabric.
Snapshots.title: Snapshots

TrafficCoverage.description:
How much of the fabric the rate window saw.

Deliberately thinner than `CounterCoverage`: there is no `unsupported`,
because PortXmitData and PortRcvData are mandatory in IBTA and no port
fabricates them, and no `sweeps`, because a rate is bounded by two readings
however many sat between them.
TrafficCoverage.title: TrafficCoverage

get.description:
Per-port error deltas over `(since, until]`, sparse.

A port is present only if a counter moved or a flag is raised; everything
absent was measured, is zero, and is trusted. `coverage` is what makes that
safe to read -- check it before believing an empty `ports`.

parameters.description: Seconds to look back before `since` for the baseline reading. 0 disables the asof baseline.
parameters.name: lookback

schema.description: Seconds to look back before `since` for the baseline reading. 0 disables the asof baseline.
schema.title: Lookback

get.description:
Per-port transmit and receive rates over a trailing window, sparse.

A rate, not a delta: `at` names the instant to read *at*, and `window` only
says how long an interval to average over. Ports below the idle floor are
omitted; ports that could not be measured are present and flagged, because
an unpolled port and an idle one must not render alike.

parameters.description: Trailing window in seconds. Defaults to three times the fabric's observed traffic cadence.
parameters.name: window

schema.title: Window

get.description: The union of both topologies, each element tagged with how it changed.

Newest first. Defaults to the last 24 hours.

Complements the diff rather than duplicating it: a diff says a link is
unchanged, this says it went down and came back forty times while nobody
was looking.
Cheap enough to poll. Refetch topology only when topology_hash moves.

Both ends expanded in place, so selecting a link is one request.

The id is the canonical GUID-ordered form; the database's own port_id
ordering never appears on the wire, so this parses without consulting it.

get.description:
The collection-run index, newest first.

Every run writes a row whether or not anything changed, so this is what
makes silence readable: a gap here is the collector being down, while a run
of `changed = false` is a fabric that genuinely did not move. Those two must
never render the same way, and only this endpoint can tell them apart.
The graph as of `at`, or now.
